newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Van Leer sees profit growth ahead.
newsitem.headline: Van Leer sees profit growth ahead.

text.p: Royal Packaging Industries Van Leer NV said on Monday it expected profit growth in the years ahead.
"The company believes it is well positioned to further increase its profitability in the coming years," Van Leer said in a statement.

It added this forecast was made under the condition that no extraordinary price turbulence will occur in the company's most important raw materials markets and that no general economic recession will be experienced in its markets.
Van Leer earlier posted 1996 net profits of 96.9 million guilders, up 22.4 percent from 1995's 79.2 million.
The company had previously forecasted 1996 full-year profit growth would match the 23 percent rise posted in the first half of the year.
Turnover grew by five percent to 4.18 billion guilders. This was the balance of a seven percent rise at consumer packagings and a 2.7 percent rise at the industrial packaging division.
"This sales growth is especially gratifying after a few years in which Van Leer showed little or no sales growth," the company said.
Van Leer added it was also positive that sales growth had been higher in the second half of 1996 than in the first. In 1995 the trend was the opposite, Van Leer said.
Turnover grew by 2.1 percent through acquisitions and 1.2 percent due to currency effects, most notably because of the U.S. dollar.

Van Leer's 1996 earnings before interest and tax rose by 12.2 percent to 225.1 million guilders with the improved profitability of the consumer packagings business being the main force behind the profit growth. Virtually all activities at this division improved in 1996, the company said.
Earnings before interest and tax of the industrial packagings division fell slightly but the second half of the year was better than the first.
Better results in the steel drum business in Europe were offset by poor results in South Africa and the U.S.
Van Leer's shares were floated on the Amsterdam Stock Exchange in May 1996. It said it had used the proceeds of this initial public offering to reduce debts.
As a result, the company's 1996 financial charges fell to 65.5 million guilders from 77.5 million in the previous year.
